description:
FOUND s492b by the Fable review of #2004 (the brief's own named break case).  PRE-EXISTING: base and tree both answer ARRAY(0x..).

  my @arr = (3, 4); my $s = sprintf(@arr);        perl "2"   PCL ARRAY(0x8)
  my $p = pack(@arr);                             perl dies "Invalid type '2' in pack"   PCL "z" (it packed the ELEMENTS)
  my @s = ("-", "x"); my $r = join(@s, "p", "q"); perl "p2q"  PCL "pARRAY(0x2)q"

THE CONTEXT IS ALREADY RIGHT.  Since #2004 the prototype route annotates sprintf's / pack's / join's first slot (`$` in `$@`) SCALAR_CTX -- verified in the emitted tree.  What is missing is the EMISSION: an aggregate LEAF (a bare `@a` / `%h` token, and by the same reading an `@{...}` / `%{...}` cast) is emitted raw whatever its annotated context is.  Nothing in ExprToCL collapses one; every consumer that needs a count does it itself (`p-scalar-=`, `p-.`, `p-scalar`), and `p-list-scalar` -- the only collapse wrapper the emitter applies, at the SLICE emitter -- is the LAST-ELEMENT rule (the comma operator), not the count.  So `p-sprintf` receives the adjustable vector and `%pcl-to-string` renders it as a ref.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG.  A generic "an aggregate leaf in SCALAR_CTX emits (p-scalar X)" rule in the leaf emitter breaks the REFERENCE slots: `push @a, 1` has its array in a `\@` slot, which by design INHERITS (perl takes the container, not a value), so in a scalar-context parent -- `my $n = push(@a, 1)` -- the array would be collapsed to its count and the push would write nowhere.  Measured: `core_arg_context` returns undef for every `\`-slot, which is exactly why the annotation leaves them alone.

THE SAFE SHAPE (not built here; ~15 lines): collapse in gen_funcall_form's ARGUMENT loop, gated on `Pl::PExpr::Config::core_arg_context($name, $i)` answering 'SCALAR' -- the same one reading the annotation pass uses, consulted at the point the EMITTER needs it (the annotation gives the context, the emitter needs "collapse this aggregate"), exactly as `_proto_parse_spec` is consulted by two sites.  A reference slot answers undef and is untouched.  The collapse form is `(p-scalar X)` (count), NOT `p-list-scalar` (last element).  Predicate for "is this an aggregate leaf": ExprToCL already has `_child_is_list_expr` / `_is_array_expr_node`; a bare Symbol whose content starts with @ or % plus the two cast shapes is the whole set.
PROBE THE BREAKING CASES: `push @a, ...` / `unshift` / `splice` in a scalar-context parent (reference slots, must NOT collapse); `scalar(@a)` (already right); `join(",", @a)` (a SLURPY slot, must stay a list); `sprintf("%s", @a)` (slurpy, list); `chmod 0755, @files` (slurpy); `open($fh, ...)`; a HASH in a scalar slot (`sprintf(%h)` -- perl gives the key count in 5.26+).
BAR: emission change => corpus-diff + emission-ab + gen bump + artifacts + the full sweep; guard rows in Pl/t/list-arg-context-01.t beside #2004's.


=== SECOND SITE (s495, Fable review of s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
The SAME leaf rule at the bind operator: `@arr =~ /re/` must match against scalar(@arr) (perl even warns "Applying pattern match to @array will act on scalar(@array)").  s492b's #2102 gives the bound operand SCALAR context and every CALL / readline / backtick operand is right now, but an ARRAY leaf still is not collapsed to its count: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s495/review/s492b/r2102b.pl, 7 rows, perl vs base vs tree -- `my @m = (@arr =~ /(\d)/)` perl 3, PCL 0 on BOTH (so not a regression); `if (@arr =~ /3/)` perl yes, PCL no; an empty array perl matches /^0$/, PCL does not.  A hash operand (`%h =~ /(\d+)/`, r2102.pl row 9) agrees with perl by luck of the row.  RARE in real code (perl warns about it) -- fix it WITH the sprintf slot, in the one place: whatever collapses an aggregate leaf under an annotated SCALAR context must serve both the funcall-argument loop and the bind operand; do not write it twice (rule 11).
subject: SILENT WRONG (#2004 residue, Fable review s494): an AGGREGATE LEAF ignores its annotated SCALAR context at emission -- `my $s = sprintf(@arr)` says ARRAY(0x8) where perl says "2" (the element COUNT is the format); same for pack(@arr)'s template slot and every other builtin $-slot fed a bare array or hash
